questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding reproduction in flowering plants is FALSE?

options.text: Reproduction may occur from fragments of stems.
Reproduction may occur from tissues separated from the plant and grown on an artificial medium.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reproduction may occur through spores.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Spores** are** reproductive structures** produced by some plants, including **ferns and mosses.**
 
• Unlike seeds, spores **do not** contain an **embryo** and are not produced by flowers.
 
• They can** germinate** into new plants under favorable conditions.
 
• Spores are produced by certain bacteria as a** self-defense mechanism.**
 
• Spore walls are **thick.**
 
• They are **resilient** to a variety of environmental factors, including** high temperatures and humidity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flowering plants **reproduce through **seeds**, which are produced by the flowers after** pollination and fertilization.**
 
• Reproduction from **fragments of stems** is called** vegetative propagation**, which is a form of **asexual reproduction**. 
 
 
• This method is commonly used in **horticulture and agriculture** to produce clones of desirable plants.
 
 
 
• Reproduction from tissues separated from the plant and grown on an artificial medium is called** tissue culture,** another form of asexual reproduction.
 
 
• This method is used in **plant breeding and genetic engineering **to produce large numbers of identical plants.

questions.question: The air bubbles shine in the water because of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​Total internal reflection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Total internal reflection**

 
 
• It is the **complete reflection of a ray of light within a medium** such as water or glass from the surrounding surfaces back into the medium.
 
• The phenomenon occurs if the **angle of incidence is greater than **a certain limiting angle, called **the critical angle**.
 
• **Examples **-
 
 
• The formation of a **mirage**.
 
• **Shining of an empty test tube** in water.
 
• **Shining of a crack in a glass vessel**.
 
• Sparkling of a **diamond**.
 
• Transmission of light rays in an **optical fibre**.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dispersion**

 
 
• Dispersion is defined as the **spreading of white light into its full spectrum of wavelengths**.
 
• Examples - 
 
 
• Rainbow formation,
 
• Petrol poured on the water will show different colours,
 
• The prism splits the light into different colours on passing through it,
 
• Dispersion of colours in soap bubbles, etc.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Diffraction**
 
 
• Diffraction is the **spreading of waves around obstacles**.
 
• **Examples **- 
 
 
• X-Ray Diffraction,
 
• Water passing from a small gap,
 
• Solar or lunar corona, sound, etc.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Reflection**
 
 
• Reflection occurs when a li**ght ray hits a surface and bounces off **and returns to the medium from which it originated.
 
• **Examples **- 
 
 
• Reflection of light in the mirror, in a water pool, glowing stars, lighting of the moon at night, etc.

questions.question: Osmosis is a diffusion movement of _________.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Osmosis:**

 
 
• Osmosis is the process by which solvent molecules pass from a solution of lower concentration to a solution of higher concentration through a semipermeable membrane.
 
• It is a passive process that takes place without any expenditure of energy.
 
• **Osmosis is the passage of water** from the region of higher concentration to the region of lower concentration through a semi-permeable membrane.
 
• A plasma membrane or a cell membrane is a semipermeable or selectively permeable membrane that lets only certain molecules pass through it while keeping other molecules
 
• Movement is controlled by the **osmolarity of two compartments**.
 
• **Sodium regulator **of extracellular osmolarity.
 
• **Potassium regulator** of intracellular osmolarity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffusion:**

 
 
• Diffusion is the process of particles moving from a highly concentrated region to a low concentrated region.
 
• The **rate of diffusion** of **gases** is **higher** when compared to liquids and solids as gases can move freely from one region to another.
 
• Diffusion is only possible if the matter moves continuously as diffusion means the moving of particles from a high concentration to a low concentration region.

questions.question: The law of octaves asserts that every eighth element has comparable properties when grouped in increasing order of their atomic masses and is also known as:
questions.solution:

__
 
• **The law of octaves,** also referred to as **Newlands' Law of Octaves, **posits that when elements are arranged in ascending order of their atomic masses, the properties of every eighth element resemble those of the first.
 
• In 1864, British scientist John Newlands endeavoured to organize the 62 known elements of his time. He arranged them based on increasing atomic weight and observed that every eighth element exhibited similar characteristics.
 
• For instance, taking the elements **Li, Be, B, C, N, O, F, and Na**, where lithium (Li) is the first element and sodium (Na) is the eighth, it was noted that the properties of sodium repeat those of lithium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] 

**Important Points__**

 
• **Gravity** is the force that attracts objects with mass toward each other. This force is directly proportional to the masses of the objects involved and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them, meaning it weakens as the distance between the objects increases.
 
• **The Doppler effect** refers to the alteration in the frequency of a wave when both the source emitting the wave and the observer detecting it are in relative motion concerning each other. This effect is commonly observed in various phenomena, including sound waves and light waves.
 
• **Coulomb's law** delineates the magnitude of the electrostatic force between two charged objects. According to this law, the force between the charges is directly proportional to the product of their magnitudes and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

questions.question: Which of the following device is based upon magnetic effect of electric current?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Electric current:**

__
 
• Electric current is the flow of electric charge in its path called circuit.
 
• The electric current has magnetic, heating, and chemical effects.

**Heating effects of current:**

 
• An electrical appliance gets heated after a few hours of use.
 
• The appliances offer resistance to the current.
 
• In overcoming the resistance heat is generated.
 
• This has many applications like an electric fuse, heater, iron, etc.

**Magnetic effect of current:**

 
• A current-carrying wire has a magnetic effect which was discovered by Hans Christian Oersted.
 
• When an electric current carrying wire is wrapped over a soft iron core, it acts as a magnet.
 
• Such kind of magnet is known as an electromagnet.
 
• If the current stops flowing, the magnetic effect vanishes.
 
• It is used in electric bells, cranes, etc.

**Explanation:**__

**Electric bell:**

__
 
• Electric bell works on the magnetic effect of current, it uses an electromagnet to produce sound.
 
• It consists of an electromagnet, striker, and gong.
 
• When the circuit is closed, the electromagnet attracts the striker towards it.
 
• The striker hits the gong and produces a sound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a3720cf3f2cc9d8ac210f2c535d95be834728a8193213f1c9ac247073b915bae.png] 

Therefore,** the electric bell device is based upon the magnetic effect of the electric current.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• In a colloid, the **dispersing medium** is the substance in which the colloidal particles are distributed.
 
• **Shaving Cream** is an example of a colloid where the **dispersing medium is a liquid** and the dispersed phase is gas, forming a foam.

• **Colloids** are mixtures where one substance is dispersed evenly throughout another at a microscopic level.
 
• They can be classified based on the **state of the dispersing medium and the dispersed phase** into various types such as sols, gels, emulsions, and foams.
 
• **Foams** are colloidal systems where a gas is dispersed in a liquid or solid. Examples include shaving cream (gas in liquid) and styrofoam (gas in solid).
 
• **Emulsions** are colloids where both the dispersing medium and the dispersed phase are liquids, such as milk or mayonnaise.
 
• **Sols** are colloids where solid particles are dispersed in a liquid, such as paint or blood.
 
• **Gels** are colloids where liquids are dispersed in solids, such as jelly or gelatin desserts.

questions.question: Jack can do a piece of work in 30 days. Ryan can do this work in 14 days. Jack started the work alone. After how many days should Ryan join him, so that the work is finished in 15 days?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Jack can complete a work in 30 days

Ryan can complete a work in 14 days

**Concept:**

Total work = Efficiency × Time Required

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be 210 units (LCM of 30 and 14)

Efficiency of Jack = 210/30 = 7 units/day

Efficiency of Ryan = 210/14 = 15 units/day

Combines efficiency of Jack and Ryan = 7 + 15 = 22

Let after 'x' days Ryan joins Jack

⇒ Jack works alone for 'x' days and for (15-x) days Jack and Ryan work together

According to the question, work is completed in 15 days

⇒ 7x + [(15-x) × 22] = 210

⇒ 7x + 330 - 22x = 210

⇒ 15x = 120

⇒ x = 8 days

questions.question: A train crosses a one km long bridge in one minute and a 750 m long tunnel in 50 seconds. Assuming the train is running at a uniform speed, what is its speed?
questions.solution:
Given:

A train crosses a one km long bridge in one minute and a 750 m long tunnel in 50 seconds.

Concept used:

One km = 1000 m

One minute = 60 sec

1m/s = 18/5 km/h

While a train crosses a platform or tunnel, it crosses the sum of its length and the length of the platform.

Calculation:

Let the length of the train be L meters and the speed of the train be S m/s.

According to the question,

(L + 1000) = S × 60 ....(1)

(L + 750) = S × 50 ....(2)

Now (1) ÷ (2),

(L + 1000)/(L + 750) = (S × 60)/(S × 50)

⇒ (L + 1000)/(L + 750) = 6/5

⇒ 6L + 4500 = 5L + 5000

⇒ L = 500

Putting the value of L in (1),

(500 + 1000) = S × 60

⇒ 1500 = S × 60

⇒ S = 1500/60

⇒ S = 25

Hence, the speed of the train = 25 m/s

Now, the speed of the train

⇒ 25 × (18/5)

⇒ 90 km/h

∴ Its speed is 90 km/h.

questions.question: A 4 kg object is lifted vertically with a force of 50 N. If the object is lifted 5 meters, how much work is done?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**250 J**__.

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• Work done : The work done by a force on an object is defined as the product of the force applied and the distance moved by the object in the direction of the force.

The formula for work done is given by:

W = F times d

Where W = work done, F = force applied, and d = distance moved by the object in the direction of the force.

CALCULATION__:

Given that:

Force (F) = 50 N

Distance (d) = 5 meters

Using the formula for work done:

W = F times d = 50 N times 5 m = 250 J

Hence, the work done in lifting the object is 250 Joules.

**​****Ureters:**

__
 
• They are muscular tubes that** transport urine from the kidneys to the urinary bladder.**
 
• They extend from the renal pelvis of the kidney to the urinary bladder.
 
• **Each kidney has one ureter**, and the urine flows through the ureters by peristaltic contractions of the smooth muscle in the ureter walls.
 
• They have an **average length of about 25–30 centimeters** (10–12 inches).
 
• They have a one-way flow mechanism facilitated by the presence of valves called ureterovesical valves, which** prevent the backflow of urine **from the bladder into the ureters.

• It is a tubular structure that **serves as a duct for the passage of urine from the urinary bladder to the outside of the body.**
 
• **In males**, the urethra also has a reproductive function, **serving as the passage for semen** during ejaculation.
 
• The length and structure of the **urethra differ between males and females.**
 
• The female urethra is shorter and primarily serves the purpose of conducting urine from the bladder to the external urethral orifice.

**Nephrons:**

 
• They are the **structural and functional units of the kidneys**, which are vital organs **responsible for filtering blood, removing waste products,** and regulating various physiological processes in the body.
 
• Each **kidney contains approximately one million nephrons,** and these microscopic structures play a crucial role in maintaining the body's internal balance by regulating water and electrolyte levels and removing metabolic waste.

questions.question: The force between two charges is 420 N. If the distance between the charges is doubled, then the force will be
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**105 N**__

__**Calculation**__

The force between two charges, according to** Coulomb's Law**, is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them. So, if the distance between the charges is doubled, the force will decrease by a factor of

{1over 2² }={1over 4 }

Given that the initial force is 420 N, when the distance is doubled, the force will be

New force= {1over 4 }times 420 = 105 N

So, when the distance between the charges is doubled, the force will be __**105 N.**__

questions.question: The angle of elevation of a ladder standing diagonally against a wall is 60° and its lower end is at a distance of 3.7 meter from the wall. Find the length of the ladder.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a 30°-60°-90° right-angled triangle, the sides opposite to the angles are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2.

The base is adjacent to 60° (opposite to 30°), so Base = 1 unit.

The hypotenuse (ladder) is opposite to 90°, so Ladder = 2 units.

Given the base, 1 unit = 3.7 m.

⇒ Ladder = 2 units = 2 × 3.7 = 7.4 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.4 meter.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Angle of elevation of the ladder (θ) = 60°

Distance from the lower end to the wall (Base) = 3.7 m

**Formula Used:**

cos(θ) = Base ÷ Hypotenuse

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b6cd246937d978c957098408e82d641b51dceb4107e826861bb59fdbde5ac55.png] 

**Calculation:**

Let the length of the ladder be L.

⇒ cos(60°) = 3.7 ÷ L

⇒ 1 ÷ 2 = 3.7 ÷ L

⇒ L = 3.7 × 2

⇒ L = 7.4 m

**∴ The correct answer is 7.4 meter.**

Angle of Elevation

It is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when viewing an object placed above the horizontal level.

Angle of Depression

It is the angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when viewing an object placed below the horizontal level. Under parallel line properties, Angle of Elevation = Angle of Depression.
